Meet your professor

Better analysis starts with a better question.

Dr. Kenechukwu Ezekwem, known to students as Prof. Ken, is a Clinical Assistant Professor of Management and Analytics at NYU's School of Professional Studies. His teaching and applied work focus on management analytics, workflow automation, decision support, and the thoughtful use of AI to improve how organizations work.

About Prof. Ken

Dr. Kenechukwu Ezekwem

Clinical Assistant Professor of Management and Analytics · NYU School of Professional Studies

He emphasizes hands-on learning: define the problem, examine the data, choose a defensible method, check the result, and explain what it supports. A chart or a statistical output is a starting point for judgment.

He holds a PhD in Transportation and Supply Chain and an MBA in Business Analytics from North Dakota State University. His published research spans transportation analytics and intelligent transit systems.

At NYU, he founded the SPS Research, Prototyping, and Production Pods (R3P), an applied AI research group where early-career analysts develop publishable research and deployable prototypes side by side. He is also Faculty Advisor to the Management & Analytics Professionals Society (MAPS).

How we learn here

Four habits for every session

01

Start with a decision

Name the stakeholder and the choice before selecting a statistical procedure.

02

Make the reasoning visible

Show counts, denominators, units, assumptions, and limits so the work can be inspected.

03

Learn through experiments

Predict the result, change an input, compare the evidence, and explain the difference.

04

Keep extending

Use the toolkit during or after the course. Build confidence at your own pace.
